# SciFork
[](https://github.com/zhang-bin-98/sci-fork/actions/workflows/release.yml) [](https://github.com/top
ics/dsh-plugin) [](LICENSE)
English | 简体中文
> Fork hypotheses. Connect evidence. Advance research.
SciFork is a biomedical **Research Graph** plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). DSH Chat stays your si
ngle conversation surface, while SciFork provides a visual Research Graph in the right sidebar to tu
rn literature findings and discussions into structured, auditable research knowledge.
> **Current release:** SciFork `0.0.8` targets DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` (desktop and same-version Web).
## What you can do
- **Deep research** — ask for deep research in DSH Chat and SciFork runs a bounded multi-level explo
ration: each level retrieves literature, records machine-reviewed Evidence, keeps every qualifying b
ranch, and automatically continues through the most promising new Hypothesis until your scope is cov

ered.
- **One-click expansion** — select any node in the graph and click **Research & Expand** for a

single grounded step outward (up to five direct candidate branches).
- **Two-stage evidence gate**
— every Evidence assertion is bound to a PMID or DOI, a source locator, and a review rationale. Mach
ine-reviewed Evidence can guide exploration, while only human-reviewed Evidence (or a validated team

Result) can support an established **Finding**.
- **Two views** — see the full research structure i
n **Main** view or focus on a single node's direct assertions in **Evidence** view, with a **Details

** panel for full Markdown notes and grouped citations.
- **Plain files + local Git** — your project
lives in ordinary local Markdown and JSON files, and every change creates a local Git checkpoint on
your current branch. You can connect the repository to GitHub or any remote of your choice.
## Views and research model
- **Main view (default)** — displays the complete research structure: starting from open **Research
Questions**, it connects candidate **Hypotheses**, testable **Predictions**, research-team **Results
**, and established **Findings**, showing how claims support, contradict, cause, or predict one anot

her.
- **Evidence view** — available whenever the selected node has direct literature support. It is
olates that node and its linked **Evidence** assertions so you can inspect the underlying literature

without visual clutter; switching back to **Main** restores your focus on that node.
- **Details pa
nel** — shows the selected item's full Markdown body, publication and review counts, and citations g
rouped into human-reviewed, machine-reviewed, rejected, and retrieval references. Click the ID at th
e top of the panel to copy it when you want to reference a specific item in Chat.
## Install and literature retrieval
**From the Plugins panel (recommended):** open **Plugins** in the DSH sidebar, select **Add plugin**
, enter `dsh-scifork@0.0.8`, install, and click **Enable now**. Pin the version explicitly: a bare n
ame installs the newest version that has passed DSH's supply-chain observation window, which can lag
newest version that has passed DSH's supply-chain observation window, which can lag a fresh release.
**From a chat:** ask the model — "install the DSH plugin `dsh-scifork@0.0.8`".
To uninstall, select **Remove** on the plugin's page; your local research project files remain intac
elect **Remove** on the plugin's page; your local research project files remain intact and readable.
### Pairing with literature retrieval
SciFork is not tied to a single database and works with real literature material in DSH Chat in this
is not tied to a single database and works with real literature material in DSH Chat in this order:
1. **Retrieval plugin (recommended)** — install `dsh-pubmed` (tested with `0.4.4`, optional) or anot

her literature/PDF plugin so the model can search papers and read abstracts automatically.
2. **Web
search** — when no retrieval plugin is installed or results are insufficient, SciFork falls back to

DSH's built-in web search.
3. **Pasted source text** — you can also paste abstracts or bounded PDF p
assages directly into Chat along with a valid PMID or DOI.
Across all paths, only records with a valid PMID or DOI and real abstract or passage text are accept
ed; title-only records are skipped and citations are never fabricated.
## Quick start
Choose an empty directory or the root of a Git repository (not a subdirectory inside another Git rep
o, and make sure Git `user.name` and `user.email` are configured). Initialize the directory once in

Then open **Research Graph** from the right-sidebar guide card or the **Research Graph** button at t
he bottom of the left sidebar:
1. **Ask a research question** — describe an open biomedical question in DSH Chat; SciFork records i

t as your starting Research Question and focuses it in the graph.
2. **Retrieve and expand** — ask D
SH to retrieve literature and import evidence; select a node and click **Research & Expand** for a s

ingle step, or ask in Chat for **deep research** to explore across multiple levels.
3. **Review and
promote** — switch between **Main** and **Evidence** views to inspect claims and sources, then ask i
n Chat to accept verified machine-reviewed assertions as human-reviewed Evidence (or critique, edit,

or delete weak branches) to advance a Hypothesis into a Finding.
4. **Check project health** — vali
date your project at any time in Chat:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The Research Graph tab is a read-only surface for browsing, focusing nodes, and triggering one-step
expansion. Day-to-day questions, deep research, edits, branch deletion, and Git history recovery all
happen in DSH Chat.
## Data and safety
SciFork runs locally and never uploads your research data or adds cloud sync. Project files store on
ly PMIDs/DOIs, article titles, journals, years, and derived assertions with locators — full abstract
s and PDFs are never written into your repository.
Before committing or sharing a project, check that it does not contain protected health information
(PHI/PII) or controlled-access data. See SECURITY.md for details.
## License
SciFork is available under the MIT License. Your research project data remains yours and may carry i
ts own ownership and sharing terms.
